main_text.l: præcellentiæ & potentiæ suam (non alienam, ut Prophetæ rem magnam facientes) atque credidisse in eum discipulos, animas suas ei, ut veraci testi, Filio Dei à Deo misso, commisisse, nec de doctrina ejus dubitasse, v. 11. dicitur.

XV. Paschatis Primi historia iter Christi ex Galilæa in Judæam, & ex Judæa in Galilæam reditum, & quæ utrobique ille gessit, complectitur. Ascendit enim Christus Hierosolymam ad Pascha, ubi Templum purgavit, & miracula satis multa edidit, Joh. II. 13–f. per discipulos baptizavit, ibid. III. 22.26. cum Nicodemo de regeneratione per aquam & Spiritum commemorabile colloquium instituit, ibid. III. 1–22. Sed audita Johannis captivitate, Judæam reliquit, & in Galilæam rediit; & Samariam transiens cum muliere Samaritana de aqua vitæ & cultu vero Dei, ibid. IV. 1–32. Et cum discipulis suis de cibo suo & messe Evangelii v. 31–39. divinos sermones cædit; credentibus in eum Samaritanis pluribus, v. 39–43. In Galilæam ubi rediit, Regnum Cœlorum prædicare perrexit, Marc. I. 14. 15. Filium Regium sanavit, Joh. IV. 46–54. Nazarethi appellens Prophetam Esajam exponit, sed mox expellitur, Luc. IV. 16–30. inde moram in Capernaum trahens, Sabbatho docet, Matth. IV. 13–18. Marc. I. 21. 22. Luc. IV. 31.32. Spiritum immundum ejicit, Marc. I. 23–28. Luc. IV. 33–37. Socrum Simonis sanat, Matth. VIII. 14. 15. Marc. I. 29–32. Luc. IV. 38.39. allatos ad se undique ægrotos curat, Matth. VIII. 16. Marc. I. 32–35. Luc. IV. 40. 41. Capernaumo relicto Galilææ urbes obambulans, in Synagogis docet, & dæmonia ejicit, Marc. I. 39. Luc. IV. 44. ex navi Simonis turbam docet, ibid. V. 1–4. miraculosam piscium capturam instituens, Simonem Petrum, Jacobum, Andream piscatores hominum facit, & passim in Synagogis docet, Matth. IV. 18–25. Marc. I. 16–20. Luc. V. 1–12. Leprosum in urbe quadam sanat, confluentibus ad eum undique pluribus, Matth. VIII. 1–4. Marc. I. 40–45. Luc. V. 12-16. iterum Capernaumi docet, & Paralytico peccata remittit, Matth. IX. 1–8. Marc. II. 1–12. Luc. V. 18–26. apud mare turbam docet, Levin seu Matthæum vocat, Matth. IX. 9. Marc. II. 13. 14. Luc. V. 27.28. in ejusdem domo se & publicanos convivantes defendit, & non jejunantes vindicat, Matth. IX. 10–13. Marc. II. 15–22. Luc. V. 29–39. Sabbatho διὰ π̔ρο̄π̔ε̄ω̄τῶ̄ transiens per sata discipulos spicas vellentes defendit, Matth. XII. 1–8. Marc. II. 23–28. Luc. VI. 1–5.

XVI. Ad Secundum Pascha Hierosolymas ascendens (Joh. V. 1.) ibidem ad piscinam Bethesdæ ægrum 38. annorum sanat, & se, quòd Deum Patrem suum nuncupasset, accurate defendit, Joh. V. 1–47. in Synagoga alio Sabbatho docet, & aridam dextram sanat, Matth. XII. 9–14. Marc. III. 1–6. Luc. VI. 6–11. Inde insidiarum metu ad mare secedens, multos sanat, Matth. XII. 15–21. Marc. III. 7–12. in montem ascendens orat, & coram discipulis & turba Divinissimam in eodem monte concionem habet, Matth. V. VI. VII. Marc. III. 13–22. Luc. VI. 12–49. Varia inde loca denuo obambulans, Capernaumi centurionis servum sanat, Matth. VIII. 5–13. Luc. VII. 1–10. in Nain

viduæ unigenitum resuscitat, ibid. II–17. in Simonis domo mulierem pedes ipsius lachrymis rigantem defendit, ibid. 36–48. Dæmoniacum sanans, se contra blasphemantes, quòd per Beelzebulem dæmonia ejiceret, defendit, Matth. XII. 22–37. Marc. III. 22–30. Signum petentibus negat in præsentiarum, & resurrectionem ex morte futuram ejus vice offert, Matth. XII. 38–45. mater, frater, soror quæ sit, ostendit, ibid. 46–50. Marc. III. 31–35. Luc. VIII. 19–22. in mari ex navigio parabolam feminantis, plurësque alias recitat, Matth. XIII. 1–53. Marc. IV. 1–34. Luc. VIII. 4–18. in ulteriorem ripam transiens mare tranquillat, ventos increpat, Matth. VIII. 18–27. Marc. IV. 35–41. Luc. VIII. 22–25. apud Gadarenos dæmonia ejicit, in porcos intrare finit, & inde Capernaum redit, Matth. VIII. 28–34. Marc. V. 1–20. Luc. VIII. 26–39. apud mare cùm esset, discipulis Johannis de jejunio respondet, filium Jairi resuscitat; hæmorrhoisan sanat, Matth. IX. 14–26. Marc. V. 21–43. Luc. VIII. 40. Inde secedens cæcis oculos aperit, dæmoniacum restituit, Matth. IX. 27–34. Urbes omnes obiens, docens, sanans, in urbem patriam redit, &c. ceu faber, ibi contemnitur, ibid. IX. 35. XIII. 54–58. Marc. VI. 1–6. commiseratus ibi turbam, messem magnam, operarios paucos, duodecim Apostolos cum mandatis ablegat, Matth. IX. 36–38. X. 1–42. Marc. VI. 7–11. Luc. IX. 1–5. qui obeuntes singulos Judææ vicos prædicant, sanant, Marc. VI. 12–16. Luc. IX. 6. quibus reversis, & Johannis audita morte discipulorumque fœctis, in desertum urbis Bethsaida cum discipulis abit, sequentibus ipsum turbis. Unde in montem subiens quinque panibus & duobus piscículis homines quinquies mille pascit, & volentibus eum Regem facere, discipulos intrare navim, & præire in ripam alteram, Capernaum versus, noctu super mare ambulat, in Gennesareth venit, ubi mox ægros allatos curat, Matth. XIV. 13. 14. Marc. VI. 31–56. Luc. IX. 10–17. Joh. VI. 1–22. ac demum Capernaumi in Synagoga de pane vitæ concionatur, & se eum esse asserit. ibid. v. 22–71.
XVII. Ad Tertii Paschatis historiam plurescula referenda sunt.

Ante omnia enim Pharisæos discipulis suis, quòd illotis manibus panem comederent, exprobrantes, aboliti prætextu traditionum Divini mandati convincit, Matth. XV. 1–20. Marc. VII. 1–23. in confinia Tyri & Sidonis secedens, Syrophœnissæ ibi filiolam à dæmonio liberat, Matth. XV. 21–28. Marc. VII. 24–30. mox ad mare Galilææ veniens surdum restituit, ibid. VII. 31–39. ibi in montem ascendens plures sanat, Matth. XV. 29–32. in deserto turbam pascit, ibid. XV. 32–38. Marc. VIII. 1–9. hinc in partes Dalmanutha seu Magdala veniens, Matth. XV. 39. Marc. VIII. 11–14. & in ulteriorem ripam abiens à fermento Pharisæorum dehortatur, Matth. XVI. 5–12. Marc. VIII. 14–21. Bethsaidæ cæcum sanat, ib. 22–26. in vicis Cæsareæ Philippi Petri confessionem audit, mortem suam prædicit, &c. Matth. XVI. 13–28. Marc. VIII. 27–38. Luc. IX. 18–27. Post dies octo in monte sublimi transfiguratur, & sequente die de monte descendens, filium lunaticum à dæmonio libe-bera-
